haiku-low.q1: It does not differ: both get a 401 login page with the same text, "Invalid email or password". For unknown emails, bcrypt still runs against a dummy hash of the same cost so timing matches.
haiku-low.q2: It gets a 429 with Retry-After and a lockout page. The password is not checked, and retries during the lockout do not extend it.
haiku-low.q3: The session that the incoming cookie pointed to is deleted, and a new session with a new random ID is created. The old ID never becomes valid again.
haiku-low.q4: Only an opaque random session ID (32 random bytes, base64url) in the __Host-sid cookie, with no user data. It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
haiku-low.q5: After 12 hours from login, counted by expires_at, which is never extended. Its next request is sent to /login without warning, even if the user was active.
haiku-low.q6: It runs a best-effort DELETE of that session row, ignoring any error, clears the cookie, and replies 303 to /login.
haiku-low.q7: It deletes the session row matching the cookie hash, then clears the cookie and replies 303 to /login. If the session is already gone, the reply is the same. A database error gives a 503 and keeps the cookie.
haiku-low.q8: In the existing shared Postgres, in the sessions table. The instance hashes the cookie ID and looks up that row, so any instance finds it.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_attempts table, one row per allowed attempt with attempt_at. The server counts rows for that email with attempt_at within the last 10 minutes, using the database now().
haiku-low.q10: It compares the id_hash, last_seen_at within 30 minutes, and expires_at in the future, all using database now(). If valid, it writes last_seen_at = now() and returns user_id.
haiku-low.q11: A 503 page, "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Please try again in a moment." No session is issued and no new cookie is set, and the old session stays.
haiku-low.q12: A periodic cleanup job, run by each instance every 5 minutes under pg_try_advisory_lock. It deletes sessions past the idle limit or expires_at, and old attempt and lockout rows.

sonnet.q1: It does not differ. Both get 401 with the login page showing exactly "Invalid email or password". No cookie is set or cleared.
sonnet.q2: It gets 429 with Retry-After and the lockout page. The password is never checked and nothing is written. Retries during a lockout do not extend it.
sonnet.q3: The old session row is deleted, in the same transaction that inserts the new session. The old ID never becomes valid again. This defeats session fixation.
sonnet.q4: Only an opaque random session ID (32 random bytes, base64url), in the cookie __Host-sid. It carries no user data. Page scripts cannot read it because the cookie is HttpOnly.
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after login, the absolute limit. Activity does not extend expires_at, so the next request after that is redirected to /login without warning.
sonnet.q6: It does a best-effort DELETE of the session row by id hash and ignores any failure of that delete. It then clears the cookie (Max-Age=0) and replies 303 to /login.
sonnet.q7: If a cookie is present, the server deletes the session row with that hash. Zero rows is fine. Then it clears the cookie and replies 303 to /login, the same reply with or without a session. If the delete errors, the user gets a 503 and the cookie is kept.
sonnet.q8: In the shared Postgres, in the sessions table. Either instance hashes the cookie's session ID (SHA-256) and looks up the row by id_hash in Postgres. No instance keeps state in memory.
sonnet.q9: In the login_attempts table in Postgres, with one row per allowed attempt, written before the password is checked. The server counts rows whose attempt_at is within the last 10 minutes, using the database now(). The locked_until value is kept separately in login_lockouts.
sonnet.q10: It compares last_seen_at against now() minus 30 minutes (idle limit) and expires_at against now() (12-hour absolute limit), using the database clock. When both pass, it sets last_seen_at = now() in the same atomic UPDATE and returns user_id.
sonnet.q11: A 503 page: "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Please try again in a moment." No session is issued. The session transaction rolls back whole, so the old session stays. The attempt row stays committed and still counts toward the limit.
sonnet.q12: A periodic cleanup job runs on each instance every 5 minutes, guarded by pg_try_advisory_lock so only one runs at a time. It deletes sessions idle for over 30 minutes or past expires_at. Expired sessions seen on a request are also deleted.
